sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:14

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:14:1
items.html: And behold, after ZON received from the root of Hochma as well, then they need suckle no more, and then ZON descend into their own vessel: That is to say, that after the coupling was made upon the coarseness of phase three, complete both in the aspect of drawing and in the aspect of clothing, the Nukva of Keter is therefore able to expand from above downward into ten Sefirot, to the Guf [body], with the light she receives from the Rosh [head]; and together with her the male of the vessel of Keter descends and expands to the Guf as well. And this is what he says, “and then ZON descend into their own vessel,” that is, the Guf.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:14:2
items.html: And then the root of Hochma is raised to her place, and the root of Keter too gathers the light to itself. This means that the matter of the descent of the degrees mentioned above, which was made in the Rosh [head], was only for the duration of the coupling; but after the coupling, and after the ZON descended into their own vessel, the degrees returned again to their place as at first, and the light of the upper Keter returned to the vessel of Keter, and the light of Hochma to the vessel of Hochma, and so forth. And even so, the upper Keter did not shine to the light of Keter that is beneath Malchut, such that it could expand to the Guf [body] as at first; rather “the root of Keter gathered the light to itself, and that Keter which is at the end of the roots receives only the vitality it needs for itself alone” — and not in such a way that it could return and expand within the Guf as at first. And the reason for the matter is as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:14:3
items.html: It reaches Keter, to the vessel. For that light of the coupling made upon the aspect of the female of Keter in the phase three of the Rosh [head], which is at the level of Hochma and clothes in the vessel of Keter, as above — it descends with the male and Nukva mentioned into the Guf [body], and clothes likewise in the vessel of Keter of the Guf. And this is what he says, “for the light returned into its own vessel,” that is, into the vessel of Keter, which belongs to the light of Hochma from the side that it was so drawn from the aspect of the coupling. And therefore it is called “it reaches Keter” of the Guf.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:14:4
items.html: The root of the upper Keter is called “it does not reach” below in Akudim. That is to say, when we say “it reaches Keter” of the Guf [body], the meaning is not that the light of Keter of the Rosh [head] shines in the Guf, for this light of Keter always “does not reach” within the Guf. Rather the meaning is the light of Hochma of the Rosh, as above, only that it clothes in the vessel of Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:14:5
items.html: Behold, we have raised, etc., Keter, and there is in it only the light of Hochma. He informs us to know that throughout this whole second expansion, when we say “the light of Keter” the meaning is only the light of Hochma; for so it has been explained here, that there is no light of Keter in the Guf [body] at all, but the light of Hochma alone, as above. Only that because it clothes in the vessel of Keter, we call it the light of Keter.
